My name may have been on the ballot, but every member of our team has played an important role in earning the continued support and confidence of the residents of Columbus. Congratulations to Tiara Ross, Deputy Chief of our Property Action Team, on her election to Columbus City Council. Tiara will be greatly missed in our office, but I’m excited for this opportunity for her to continue to serve and make an impact.

Together, our office is making a real difference in people’s lives and moving Columbus towards becoming the next great American city. Let’s keep it up.

item.title: City Attorney Zach Klein News Recap | October 2025
item.description:
The latest news from the Columbus City Attorney’s Office—October 2025

Columbus sued major corporations that knowingly produced dangerous chemicals that have negative impacts on the environment and public health—and won. As part of the settlement, Columbus received $4 million from the 3M Corporation, the first of several large payments as the litigation continues.

  • ABC6: 3M Corporation pays $4 million to Columbus in 'forever chemical' lawsuit settlement

  • 10TV: Columbus receives $4 million in initial settlement funds from lawsuit over 'forever chemicals'

  • The Columbus Dispatch: 3M to pay Columbus $4 million in settlement over forever chemical contamination

City Attorney Klein recently penned an Op-Ed in the Dispatch calling on Donald Trump to get serious about domestic violence because survivors and their families deserve leaders who take them seriously and invest in supports to help them break the cycle of violence and thrive.

  • The Columbus Dispatch: Domestic violence not a 'little fight.' Columbus survivors need Trump to get it. | Opinion

Earlier this month, City Attorney Klein joined civic and community partners, advocates and survivors to shine a light on domestic violence, illuminating City Hall to mark the start of Domestic Violence Awareness Month. 

  • ABC6: 'Enough is enough,' Columbus domestic violence survivors and supporters speak out

  • The Columbus Dispatch: Columbus, community partners hold third annual vigil honoring domestic violence victims

  • 10TV: Columbus city leaders take a data-driven approach to address domestic violence

A bipartisan group of state lawmakers introduced a resolution urging Ohioans to safely store their guns in homes with children. City Attorney Klein applauded the effort, and urged lawmakers to do more to help keep our kids and communities safe.

  • WEWS (Cleveland): Ohio lawmakers urging residents to safely store guns amid rising child deaths

Columbus’ Community Immersion Program was named a NewDEAL Ideas Challenge finalist, a prestigious nomination that highlights the best of the best policies that are changing communities across America. The 5-year-old program immerses new police officers in the communities they’ll patrol, allowing them to get to know the neighborhood and improve community-police relations. 

  • NewDEAL: NewDEAL Forum Announces Ideas Challenge Finalists, Recognizing Innovative Policies

City Attorney Klein and Anti-Domestic Violence Group Leader Share Emotional Moment

Join us on Tuesday, October 21st, at 11:00 a.m. for a Big Table conversation about the mounting cost of domestic violence and the impact on agencies and nonprofits that provide vital support to survivors in our community.

item.title: Donald Trump talks tough on crime until it comes to domestic violence.
item.description:
Donald Trump Must Join the Fight Against Domestic Violence

In my office, domestic abuse cases are the most serious crimes we prosecute, and unfortunately, Columbus’ domestic violence and stalking unit handles thousands of these cases each year.

Many involve severe bodily harm and violence I wouldn’t wish on my worst enemy. That’s why we took the unprecedented step to push for $500,000 bonds for the worst offenders, those who pose the greatest risk for more lethal violence to their victims.

Domestic violence is heinous and must be treated that way—with tough prosecutions, harsh sentences and total condemnation from our leaders, from local prosecutors up to the president. That’s why for the survivors and families of those lost to domestic violence who gathered at city hall this week for Domestic Violence Awareness Month, President Donald Trump’s comments in September downplaying the severity of domestic violence cut especially deep.

Read more

Where would you seek domestic violence support?

Take a quick, five question survey to help us improve access to domestic violence support in Columbus and Franklin County.

item.title: City Attorney Zach Klein Newsletter | September 2025
item.description:
September 2025

Last weekend, I spoke at the Department of Neighborhoods’ annual Best Practices conference. In my remarks, I talked about the importance of being a good neighbor, especially in times like these. Caring, listening, and showing up for each other can make a big difference.

I’ve always believed that real change starts close to home, right here in our own neighborhoods. Together, we can strengthen our city—and our country—to reflect the best of who we are.

October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month. On Wednesday, October 1st, we’ll gather at City Hall at 6 PM to shine a light on domestic violence—honoring survivors; remembering the lives lost; and recognizing the advocates, prosecutors, and police officers who work tirelessly to deliver hope, healing, and justice. I hope to see you there.

3M Corporation pays out millions of dollars to Columbus as part of forever chemical lawsuit settlement

City Attorney Zach Klein announced the City received $4 million in initial settlement funds stemming from its lawsuit against several major chemical companies for their negligence in the production of forever chemicals, dangerous synthetic compounds created by these companies that are found in many everyday household items and now the environment, which have been linked to numerous health issues.

“Corporations like 3M knew the dangers of producing forever chemicals, did nothing to protect consumers or the environment, and now are being held accountable for their negligence. This settlement ensures that these companies—not ratepayers—are on the hook for cleaning up the mess they made,” said City Attorney Klein.

item.title: City Attorney Office Bulletin | September 2024
item.description:
September 2024

Team,

I can’t believe it’s already September. August seemed to fly by, and it was nothing short of eventful. Despite ongoing challenges caused by the recent cyber attack on the City’s IT systems, our office moved full steam ahead on many key priorities, from cracking down on dangerous drug houses and problem properties to reaching a historic agreement to finally fix our state’s broken criminal background check system.

If you haven’t already, I strongly encourage you to freeze your credit, and enroll yourself and others in your household in Experian credit monitoring. This includes two years of free credit monitoring and $1 million of protection against fraud and identity theft. The deadline to enroll is November 29, and service begins upon enrollment. Learn more about enrolling and bolstering your own cybersecurity at columbus.gov/cyber.

Keep up the great work.

  • Elizabeth Agranovsky, Legal Intake Counselor
  • Emily Buchanan, Legal Advocate
  • Audrey Haring, Legal Intake Counselor (Property Action Team)

item.title: City Attorney Office Bulletin | August 2024
item.description:
August 2024

Team,

The past few weeks have been challenging. The City experienced a cybersecurity incident and we’re still waiting for some of our systems to come back online. While the lack of internet and connectivity has made our work more difficult at times, it hasn’t stopped us from delivering results for Columbus residents and families. Just last month, the City Attorney’s Office:

  • announced proactive steps to hold drug companies and pharmacy pricing middlemen accountable for artificially inflating the price of insulin.
  • resolved an anti-LGBTQ+ bias crime where a defendant was caught urinating on a pride flag.
  • supported legislation from Columbus City Council to do more to hold negligent landlords accountable and crack down even further on street racing and reckless driving.
  • continued to prosecute criminal cases, provide timely counsel to our clients, and make real strides on our priorities as an office.

This past month, we also had a strong presence at OMAA’s 2024 Municipal Law Institute. Thank you to those who presented: Lara Baker-Morrish, Soogie Choi, Rich Coglianese, Alexis Dorsey, Steve Dunbar, Jeff Furbee, Amy Musto, Andres Olivari, David Pelletier, Tiara Ross, and Matt Sturtz.

None of this would be possible without you. Thank you all for your patience and flexibility during this time. I’m especially grateful to our IT department and friends at DOT who have been working hard to secure our systems and bring us back online.

Keep up the great work, everyone.

item.title: City Attorney Office Bulletin | July 2024
item.description:
July 2024

Team,

Yesterday, our nation celebrated 248 years of independence. While this is a great nation, I have serious concerns about the future of our democracy. Like many of you, I’m troubled by recent Supreme Court rulings and acutely aware of the stakes of the upcoming election. Time and time again, we’re reminded that our democracy is fragile, and our systems are imperfect.

As Columbus City Attorney, I will always defend democracy and the rule of law despite the challenges we face here in our state and nationally. I’m grateful to serve alongside dedicated public servants like yourselves who prove each and every day that government can deliver meaningful results and affect positive change.

If you haven’t yet, I hope each of you can take a moment to look back and feel proud of what we’ve accomplished during the first half of this year. There’s much more to do, and I look forward to continuing to work together to strengthen Columbus neighborhoods and protect public health and safety.

Keep up the great work.
